==================
newlines: statements end at newlines
==================

fn main() {
    let x = 1
    let y = 2
    print("{x + y}")
}

---

  (function_declaration
    name: (identifier)
    parameters: (parameter_list)
    body: (block
      (block_lbrace)
      (let_statement
        pattern: (pattern
          (binding_pattern
            name: (identifier)))
        value: (integer_literal))
      (let_statement
        pattern: (pattern
          (binding_pattern
            name: (identifier)))
        value: (integer_literal))
      (expression_statement
        expression: (call_expression
          function: (identifier)
          arguments: (arguments
            (argument
              value: (string
                (interpolation
                  value: (additive_expression
                    left: (identifier)
                    right: (identifier))))))))
      (rbrace))))

==================
newlines: same-line statements are an error
==================

fn main() { let x = 1 let y = 2 }

---

            (integer_literal))
          (rbrace))))


==================
newlines: continuation after operators and punctuation
==================

fn main() {
    let a = 1 +
        2
    let b = [1,
        2]
    let c = (1
        + 2)
    let d = foo(1,
        2)
}

fn foo(a: int, b: int) -> int { a + b }

==================
newlines: continuation before dot else and or coalesce
==================

fn main() {
    let value = Some(1)
        .unwrap_or(0)
    let other = if value > 0 { 1 }
        else { 2 }
    let flag = true
        and false
    let fallback = None
        ?? 7
}

==================
newlines: newlines are ignored in list-style braces
==================

struct Point {
    x: int,
    y: int,
}

enum Shade {
    Light,
    Dark,
}

fn main() {
    let p = Point {
        x: 1,
        y: 2,
    }
    let table = {
        "a": 1,
        "b": 2,
    }
    match p.x {
        1 => print("one"),
        _ => print("other"),
    }
}

---

==================
newlines: blocks inside parentheses
==================

fn main() {
    let values = [1, 2]
    let mapped = values.map(fn(x) {
        let y = x + 1
        y
    })
    print("{mapped.len()}")
}

==================

==================
newlines: missing comma between match expression arms
==================

fn choose(x: int) -> int {
    match x {
        1 => 10
        2 => 20,
        _ => 0,
    }
}
